target_customer: Private medical practices that run prior authorizations through EHRs such as eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen and ModMed
problem: Prior authorization is slow manual work for small practices, with payer follow up and denial appeals eating staff time and revenue.
business_model: B2B SaaS for prior authorization automation (pricing not found)

founders.name: Nami Lindquist
education: University of Pennsylvania, Management and Technology (M&T) undergraduate
founders.background_notes: From Bellevue, WA per YC page; employers not listed.

competitors.name: Innovaccer Flow Auth
competitors.what: prior auth from eligibility to appeals, aimed at larger organizations

competitors.name: Develop Health
competitors.what: GenAI prior authorization and medication access

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs EHR integrations, payer portal workflows, appeals writing and accurate clinical documentation, with healthcare data handling.

defensibility.rationale: EHR integration and stored approval records create some lock-in, but several funded rivals address the same task.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Innovaccer launched a competing prior auth product in August 2025; no acquisition of ClaimGlide found.

market_need_then: Prior authorization burden is a long standing complaint of practices, and 2025 saw many launches and raises aimed at it; a CMS electronic prior authorization requirement is mentioned for 2026 (not verified).

identity.logo: Vertical ClaimGlide logo in the site header
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, benefit focused and reassuring; replies within a day.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive compound name that conveys smooth claims, but no brand press or community found.

outcome_analysis: ClaimGlide is a one person Winter 2026 YC company automating prior authorization for private practices. It is too early for an outcome. The solo team, many funded rivals including Innovaccer and Develop Health, and no named customers on the site are the main uncertainties.
notes: Funding: VCBacked and PitchBook both list about $500k with YC as the only investor, but both are aggregators, no Form D found, and the amount is likely the standard YC deal; not recorded as a round. Claim Health and ClaimSorted are different companies. Competitor sources are 2025 and early 2026. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed (March 2026, Y Combinator the only investor) is recorded from VCBacked, with PitchBook also listing $500K with YC as sole investor; it rests on aggregators and may be the standard YC deal. No press release found.
